🚑 Account Rescue: When Things Go Wrong · Lesson 3 of 6

Reach Crashed? Diagnose a 'Shadowban' Before You Panic

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

Instagram has a screen that tells you, in plain words, whether your posts can be shown to people who don't follow you. Most creators who complain about a 'shadowban' have never opened it.

Mosseri has said 'shadowbanning is not a thing'. Platforms do limit reach, though. They just use different names: Instagram says content is 'not eligible to be recommended', and TikTok calls it 'ineligible for the For You feed'. The good news is that both now tell you when it happens, if you know where to look.

90 days
how long a TikTok strike stays on your record before it expires. Hitting a strike threshold in one policy or feature can mean a permanent ban (TikTok, 2023, via Dhaka Tribune)

The 10-minute diagnosis

  1. Instagram: Settings > Account > Account Status (professional accounts; menus vary by app version). Check whether your content can be recommended to non-followers.
  2. TikTok: open Account status or Account check in the Safety Center. Account check reviews your last 30 posts and shows any restrictions on comments or messages.
  3. YouTube: Studio > Analytics > Reach. If impressions fell, distribution changed. If impressions held but click-through fell, your titles and thumbnails stopped working.
  4. Compare against your own normal. Use the middle result of your last 10 posts, not your one viral hit.
  5. Split followers vs non-followers in Insights. That split usually tells you whether it's a restriction or just a weak post.
PlatformWhere to checkWhat a restriction looks likeHow to fix
InstagramSettings > Account > Account Status'Not eligible to be recommended', with example posts or profile partsEdit or delete the flagged item, or tap Request a review
TikTokSafety Center > Account status / Account checkA notice that your account is ineligible for the For You feed. Content also gets harder to find in searchAppeal from the notice, and stop posting the type of content that was flagged
YouTubeStudio > Analytics > Reach; Studio > Content > Restrictions columnNo 'status' screen for reach. Look for copyright or ad-suitability restrictions on specific videosFix the restriction, or check whether the drop is impressions or click-through
EndaViralMy Orders, then a ticket with the order IDDelivered followers or likes dropping after an orderAsk support what the service covers. Don't re-order to 'top up'
💡 The signature of a real restriction

Instagram says content that breaks its Recommendation Guidelines can still reach your followers normally. It just isn't shown to strangers. So steady reach from followers with non-follower reach near zero across several posts points to a restriction. Both numbers falling together usually means the content, the timing or the season.

When it's just normal variance

  • A viral outlier reset your expectations. One Reel at 80,000 views makes 4,000 feel like a ban. It isn't.
  • The calendar. Exam season, January, a big news week or an election cycle all change what Kenyans are scrolling.
  • Your topic drifted. Instagram now lets viewers adjust their own topics, so off-niche posts land with fewer of the right people.
  • Removed fake activity. If you've ever bought engagement, platforms remove inauthentic likes and follows they detect. A drop in those numbers is a clean-up, not a shadowban.
Fixes and realistic timelines

There's no official clock for getting recommendations back. Instagram only says an account-wide restriction lasts 'for a period of time', and TikTok calls For You ineligibility 'temporary'. What you control: remove or edit flagged posts, appeal genuine mistakes, and post clean, on-niche content on a steady rhythm. Deleting your whole grid or going silent for weeks doesn't reset anything.

⚡ Quick check

Your last six Reels reached your followers as usual, but reach to non-followers fell to almost nothing. What's the most likely explanation?

Instagram says content that breaks its Recommendation Guidelines still reaches followers but isn't recommended to non-followers. Account Status shows whether that's happening and lets you fix it or request a review.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. 'Shadowban' has official names: not eligible for recommendations (Instagram), ineligible for For You (TikTok).
  2. Check Account Status and Account check before you change anything.
  3. Followers steady, non-followers near zero: likely a restriction. Both falling: usually content or season.
  4. TikTok strikes expire after 90 days. Fix, appeal, and keep posting clean content.
